lesson_title: Big Gear Slow, Small Gear Fast
hook_text: Two plastic gears and a marker dot explain how a motor the size of your fist lifts a cage of eighty miners.
clip_script: Teeth pass one for one where two gears meet. So a 10-tooth gear turning a 40-tooth gear has to go round four times for the big one to go round once. Velocity ratio: driven teeth over driver teeth, 40 over 10, four to one. And meshed gears always turn opposite ways. Now the trade: whatever gears do to speed, they do the opposite to force. The big gear turns a quarter as fast and four times as hard. Mechanical advantage four. Small driving big: slow and strong, MA above one. Big driving small: fast and weak, MA below one, like a bicycle on the flat. Nothing is free: four times the force, a quarter of the distance. That is why the winder has a gearbox: fast weak motor in, slow strong drum out, and a cage that rises at a safe speed.
visual_style: Two gears mesh on a whiteboard pegboard with marker dots; turn counters tick 4 and 1; arrows show opposite rotation; a force arrow grows on the big gear as a speed arrow shrinks; a motor-gearbox-drum chain lights up.
pacing: One for one, the ratio, opposite directions, the trade, the winder.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the teeth on any two gears you can find to work out their ratio.
